theses.worldView: For the next two years global oil, gas and copper supply grows slower than demand because a decade of underinvestment, long project lead times and producer discipline keep the commodity cycle firm; energy and materials firms therefore convert high asset utilization into durable free cash flow rather than into ruinous new supply.
theses.portfolioExpression: Roughly 20% of capital goes to integrated energy (XOM, CVX), oilfield services (SLB) and copper (FCX) as direct beneficiaries of that supply constraint, plus BRK-B which owns one of the largest US energy footprints inside a fortress balance sheet.

theses.title: Investors rotate from long-duration growth toward balance-sheet strength and tangible cash flows
theses.worldView: After the AI-led growth run, several crowded software and mega-cap growth names in the snapshot are down 25-55% from their 52-week highs (e.g. ORCL -53% over 12 months, GOOG -26% over 3 months) while energy, financials and value factors have led; over 24 months capital reprices toward book-value anchors, normalized bank earnings and diversified industrial cash flows rather than long-duration narratives.
theses.portfolioExpression: JPM, BAC and Citigroup plus the VTV value-factor ETF express the rotation at the aggregate level, with BRK-B as the anchor holding that owns cash-generative operating businesses at insurance-float economics.

theses.title: Aging populations and cost-conscious consumers sustain utilization and staples volumes
theses.worldView: Demographics and persistent cost-of-living pressure mean healthcare utilization, prescription volumes and everyday staples keep growing in real terms; regulatory pricing risk is a known and largely priced-in headwind, so cash-generative pharma, managed care and staples franchises at moderate prices outperform over two years if policy stays within historical bounds.
theses.portfolioExpression: PFE, MRK, CVS and UNH express healthcare utilization and post-repricing value, while KO, MCD and PEP express staples and affordable-indulgence pricing power as ballast against cyclical drawdowns.

theses.title: Large fiscal deficits and great-power competition keep a bid under hard assets and defense
theses.worldView: Sustained government borrowing and a contested geopolitical order keep real asset prices supported and defense budgets elevated; gold, defense primes and a small monetary-network allocation (BTC) diversify equity and currency risk over two years.
theses.portfolioExpression: LMT (4%) captures elevated defense procurement, GLD (5%) is the hard-asset and currency-debasement hedge, and BTC-USD.CC at 3% is a small, explicitly speculative application of the monetary-debasement view.

pick.thesis: This 24-month medium-risk book is built on four linked world views: constrained commodity supply keeps energy and materials cash flows strong; expensive long-duration growth continues to lose leadership to balance-sheet value; utilization-driven healthcare and staples growth offers resilient returns at already-repriced prices; and persistent fiscal deficits plus geopolitics sustain hard assets and defense. Energy (20%) and financials/value (21%) provide the upside from cyclicals and mean reversion, consumer/healthcare defensives (25%) and gold (5%) provide resilience, a 9% BRK-B anchor plus a 7% VTV sleeve diversify single-name risk, BTC is capped at 3% as a deliberate speculative satellite, and 9% cash acknowledges that the snapshot shows many defensive names near 52-week highs and that entry prices here are not obviously cheap across the board.

forecasts.reason: For this +16% two-year total return to be plausible, the world must deliver a soft-ish landing in which commodity supply stays tight (supporting the energy and copper sleeves), bank credit stays benign so financials re-rate toward book value, healthcare utilization grows while pricing policy stays within historical bounds, and fiscal deficits keep gold and defense supported; the return is anchored by dividends and cash-flow compounding across cyclical and defensive sleeves, offset partly by 9% cash earning zero and by the possibility that AI-driven growth resumes leadership and this value tilt lags SPY, so the realized outcome could plausibly range from about -15% to +35%.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway Class B
positions.thesis: A conglomerate of insurance, railroads, energy utilities and a large equity portfolio with a fortress balance sheet, it is the anchor application of the value-rotation thesis: it owns tangible cash-generative businesses at insurance-float economics, and its BNSF and Berkshire Hathaway Energy units (including a large oil and gas operation) also apply the constrained-supply energy thesis even though the shares sit near their 52-week high of 556.11. The durable mechanism is compounding of operating earnings plus a huge cash pile that can buy assets in a stressed market, and its 9% weight is sized as the portfolio's stabilizing core rather than a growth bet.
positions.catalyst: Deploying its cash hoard into acquisitions or buybacks during a market drawdown, plus continued energy segment cash generation, could unlock value.
positions.invalidation: A sustained market melt-up that leaves value anchors behind, or major insurance or railroad losses, would show the world thesis is wrong or mistimed.

positions.name: Exxon Mobil
positions.thesis: An integrated oil major with upstream, downstream and chemicals assets, it is the largest direct application of the constrained-supply thesis: if the commodity cycle stays firm because of underinvestment and producer discipline, integrated majors convert high utilization into free cash flow and buybacks, and XOM is up roughly 61% over 12 months to 179.67, which I interpret as confirmation of the cycle rather than an exhausted trend (this interpretation is an assumption). The 7% size gives real cyclical upside without letting one commodity name dominate the medium-risk book.
positions.catalyst: Sustained firm crude prices, further buybacks and Permian and Guyana production growth.
positions.invalidation: A demand-led recession that pushes crude sharply lower for a year, or a wave of OPEC+ supply that breaks the cycle, invalidates both the thesis and this holding.

positions.name: Chevron
positions.thesis: The other major integrated US oil company, held alongside XOM to avoid single-operator risk inside the same world view about constrained supply: at 227.77, up about 54% over 12 months and 21% over 3 months, it is an application of the thesis that energy cash flows remain strong, with diversified upstream assets and downstream refining providing partial insulation from crude swings. Its 5% weight is smaller than XOM's purely to keep total energy concentration at a medium-risk level.
positions.catalyst: Firm refining margins and Gulf of Mexico and Tengiz project cash flow.
positions.invalidation: Sustained low crude and refining margins caused by weak demand would break the supply-constraint story for this holding.

positions.name: SLB (Schlumberger)
positions.thesis: The largest global oilfield services provider, it is the picks-and-shovels expression of the same constrained-supply world view: if producers must develop longer-life, harder projects to keep output flat, service intensity and pricing rise even if crude is merely stable. At 52.31, up about 48% over 12 months, the mechanism is operating leverage on international and offshore activity; its 4% size recognizes that services are more cyclical than integrated majors.
positions.catalyst: Rising international and offshore drilling budgets and stronger service pricing.
positions.invalidation: A capital-expenditure freeze across producers, or crude collapsing below breakeven levels for new projects, invalidates the application.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.thesis: A leading copper producer, it applies the same constrained-supply thesis to metals: electrification and grid buildout demand for copper meets long mine lead times and grade decline, so copper prices stay supported over two years. At 62.97 (up about 52% over 12 months) the mechanism is leverage from existing low-cost mines; the 4% size reflects that this is the most commodity-price-sensitive holding in the book.
positions.catalyst: Higher copper prices from electrification demand and constrained mine supply.
positions.invalidation: A Chinese-led industrial recession or a wave of new mine supply that pushes copper down persistently would break the thesis for this holding.

positions.name: JPMorgan Chase
positions.thesis: The largest US universal bank, it is the core financial application of the value-rotation thesis: if capital reprices toward tangible earnings and normalized credit rather than long-duration growth narratives, diversified banks with deposit franchises and fee businesses gain, and JPM at 340.58 (flat-to-weak over 3 months at -4%) offers a moderate entry relative to the cycle. The mechanism is net interest income plus fee income compounding; 6% is the largest single equity weight after BRK-B because the thesis needs meaningful financial exposure but not bank-sector concentration.
positions.catalyst: Stable or steeper yield curve and continued deposit growth supporting net interest income.
positions.invalidation: A credit-cycle turn with rising charge-offs, or growth resuming leadership so value lags, invalidates the thesis here.

positions.name: Bank of America
positions.thesis: A large consumer and commercial bank, it is the higher-beta application of the same rotation thesis: at 49.57, down about 21% over 3 months while its 12-month return is roughly flat, the price path suggests sentiment is already cautious on the rate-sensitive balance sheet, which is exactly where a value re-rating would start if credit holds. The mechanism is deposit franchise value and securities-portfolio mark recovery as rates stabilize; the 4% weight reflects higher interest-rate sensitivity than JPM.
positions.catalyst: Yield-curve normalization and credit costs staying benign, lifting book-value confidence.
positions.invalidation: Rising loan losses or another rate shock that deepens securities losses would invalidate the re-rating case.

positions.name: Citigroup
positions.thesis: A global bank in a multi-year simplification and restructuring, it is the deep-value application of the rotation thesis: at 123.10, off about 10% over 3 months but up about 26% over 12 months, the mechanism is a return-on-tangible-common-equity improvement from exiting non-core businesses while the stock trades on a discounted book-value narrative (the discount itself is an assumption I cannot verify without multiples). The 3% weight is deliberately small because turnaround execution risk is higher than at JPM or BAC.
positions.catalyst: Continued divestitures and cost reduction driving return on tangible common equity toward targets.
positions.invalidation: Stalled restructuring or unexpected legal and credit costs would show the value story is not materializing.

positions.name: Vanguard Value ETF
positions.thesis: A diversified US large- and mid-cap value index fund, it is the aggregate expression of the value-rotation thesis rather than any single story: it holds cheap cash-flow sectors broadly (financials, energy, healthcare, staples) so the book earns the factor tilt even if my individual stock picks are wrong. At 228.57, near its 52-week high and up about 26% over 12 months, it is not deep value, but the mechanism is factor diversification at low idiosyncratic risk; its 8% weight is sized as a portfolio-wide tilt toward the thesis.
positions.catalyst: Broad rotation of institutional flows from growth to value factors.
positions.invalidation: A renewed growth-led bull market in which value factors lag persistently for two years would invalidate the tilt.

positions.name: Pfizer
positions.thesis: A large diversified pharmaceutical company, it is the post-repricing application of the healthcare-utilization thesis: at 30.67, exactly at its 52-week high and up about 35% over 12 months after a long de-rating, the price path suggests the worst of the post-pandemic revenue and pipeline skepticism is priced, while demographics and prescription volumes keep underlying demand growing. The mechanism is oncology and specialty pipeline conversion plus cost restructuring; 5% is a full but not dominant healthcare weight within the medium-risk objective.
positions.catalyst: Oncology pipeline readouts and successful cost reductions rebuilding earnings.
positions.invalidation: Pipeline failures or aggressive government drug-pricing caps would invalidate both the holding and the thesis application.

positions.name: CVS Health
positions.thesis: An integrated pharmacy, pharmacy-benefit manager and health insurer, it applies the utilization thesis as a turnaround: at 88.51, down about 15% over 3 months though up about 19% over 12 months, the price path reflects managed-care margin pressure that I assume is largely cyclical and priced, while aging demographics keep prescription and care volumes rising. The mechanism is stabilizing Aetna medical costs plus retail pharmacy scale; the 5% weight balances attractive asymmetric upside against real execution risk in the insurance segment.
positions.catalyst: Medical cost ratio normalization in the insurance unit and retail pharmacy margin recovery.
positions.invalidation: Sustained medical cost inflation or regulatory reimbursement cuts would show the repricing assumption was wrong.

positions.name: UnitedHealth Group
positions.thesis: The largest US health insurer and health-services platform (Optum), it applies the same utilization world view from the strongest franchise in managed care: at 400.44, roughly 8% below its 52-week high and up about 19% over 12 months, the mechanism is long-run enrollment growth and services margin as utilization rises with demographics, with the current discount representing policy and medical-cost uncertainty I assume is temporary. The 5% weight matches CVS so healthcare total exposure is diversified across payer, PBM and pharma rather than concentrated in one business model.
positions.catalyst: Medical cost trends stabilizing and Optum services growth reaccelerating.
positions.invalidation: Structural regulatory changes to Medicare Advantage reimbursement or persistent medical cost overrun would invalidate the application.

positions.name: Merck & Co.
positions.thesis: A large pharmaceutical company with a leading oncology franchise, it applies the utilization thesis as defensive growth: at 148.36, up about 77% over 12 months and near its 52-week high, I hold it as a quality complement to PFE rather than a deep-value bet, on the assumption that prescription volume growth from aging populations continues and pipeline diversification offsets key-drug patent expiry. The 3% weight is intentionally modest because the strong 12-month run means less margin of safety than PFE.
positions.catalyst: Pipeline approvals and new oncology indications extending revenue growth past patent cliffs.
positions.invalidation: Key franchise patent erosion faster than pipeline replacement, or drug-pricing legislation, would invalidate the defensive-growth case.

positions.name: Coca-Cola
positions.thesis: The global non-alcoholic beverage leader with unmatched distribution, it is the staples expression of the defensive thesis: under cost-of-living pressure consumers trade toward affordable treats, and pricing power plus global volume growth protect real cash flows. At 95.83, exactly at its 52-week high and up about 43% over 12 months, the shares are not cheap on momentum alone, so the holding is sized at 5% as ballast and income stability within the medium-risk book, not as the main upside engine.
positions.catalyst: Continued pricing power and volume growth in emerging markets.
positions.invalidation: Sustained margin compression from input costs or a consumer downturn deep enough to cut volumes would break the defensive case.

positions.name: McDonald's
positions.thesis: The largest global quick-service restaurant system, it applies the same cost-of-living world view: value menus and franchised royalty economics make it a share-gainer when consumers trade down from casual dining. At 265.64, down about 10% over 12 months and near the low end of its 52-week range (230.88-334.50), the price path offers a more favorable entry than KO, which is why it earns a 3% position despite similar defensive qualities.
positions.catalyst: Value-menu traffic gains and international unit growth re-rating the franchise.
positions.invalidation: Persistent same-store sales declines showing the trade-down thesis is not working would invalidate it.

positions.name: PepsiCo
positions.thesis: A global snacks and beverages company, it diversifies the defensive sleeve across both categories and geographies: at 140.42, down about 1% over 12 months and off its 52-week high of 165.45, the mechanism is pricing power plus convenience-snack resilience under consumer pressure, and the muted price action gives a reasonable entry compared with KO. The 3% weight keeps staples as a stabilizer rather than the core of expected returns.
positions.catalyst: Volume recovery as pricing lapses, plus productivity savings supporting margins.
positions.invalidation: Sustained volume declines that show pricing has exhausted consumer willingness to pay would invalidate the application.

positions.name: Lockheed Martin
positions.thesis: The largest US defense prime, it is the direct industrial application of the geopolitical thesis: great-power competition keeps US and allied procurement elevated over two years, and long-duration programs give revenue visibility rare in industrials. At 643.15, up about 35% over 12 months but off its 52-week high of 668.17, the mechanism is funded backlog converting to cash flow; the 4% size treats it as a diversifier with lower correlation to consumer and financial cycles.
positions.catalyst: Higher defense budgets and program awards such as missiles and air defense replenishment.
positions.invalidation: Fiscal consolidation that cuts defense procurement, or major program cost overruns, would invalidate the thesis.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: A physically backed gold ETF, it is the hard-asset application of the fiscal-debasement thesis: sustained government deficits and geopolitical hedging demand keep a bid under gold even as its 12-month return is slightly negative (-2.3% at 361.65) and it sits below its 52-week high of 495.90, which I read as a better entry than chasing momentum. Gold carries no earnings, so the mechanism is purely portfolio diversification against equity and currency risk; the 5% weight is sized as a hedge, not a return engine.
positions.catalyst: Renewed central-bank buying or a fiscal stress event repricing monetary hedges.
positions.invalidation: Real fiscal consolidation plus rising real yields that durably depress gold would show the debasement view is wrong.

positions.name: Bitcoin spot pair
positions.thesis: Bitcoin is a scarce, decentralized monetary network held as the smallest, explicitly speculative application of the debasement thesis: if fiat deficits persist and institutional adoption of a capped-supply asset continues, it diversifies like digital gold over a two-year horizon. At 76,513 (up about 19% over 12 months, roughly flat over 3 months), the exposure is capped at 3% because its drawdown history is severe, its adoption and regulatory assumptions are unverifiable from this packet, and the portfolio must not depend on it.
positions.catalyst: Continued institutional and ETF-based adoption alongside persistent deficit financing.
positions.invalidation: Severe regulatory restriction, a security failure, or a durable collapse in network adoption would invalidate this application and would cost the portfolio at most 3%.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: The frozen packet gives only prices, 3- and 12-month returns and 52-week ranges; I have no valuation multiples, earnings, balance sheets, oil prices, interest rates or policy news as of the 2026-11-02 cutoff, and my general knowledge ends well before that date, so I cannot verify why MRNA is up roughly 685% over 12 months, why several software names fell 25-55%, or whether the energy leadership reflects prices, volumes or one-off events. All sector 'cheapness' arguments are therefore assumptions inferred from price paths rather than verified fundamentals, and the 22% drawdown and 16% return figures are judgmental estimates with wide uncertainty, not computed forecasts.

strategies.riskRationale: A 24-month horizon lets me accept meaningful interim volatility in exchange for diversified exposure to cash-generative value sectors, so the book blends energy cash flows (20%), financials and value-factor ETFs (21%), defensive consumer and healthcare franchises (25%), hard-asset and defense diversifiers (12%), a large diversified anchor (BRK-B 9%), and 9% cash. This is balanced rather than capital-preserving: I expect a plausible peak-to-trough drawdown near 22%, roughly in line with an equity market drawdown, because the largest sleeves (energy, financials, value factor) are economically sensitive while staples, pharma, gold and cash cushion the downside, and no single speculative outcome (including the 3% BTC sleeve) is required for the thesis to work.

pick.risks: Main risks: a hard global recession crushes energy prices and semicap orders simultaneously, making T1 and T2 correlated losers; a second AI capex bust could cut AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, TSM and GOOGL another 30-40%; energy is roughly 23% concentrated in one sector with commodity beta; crypto (12%) is extremely volatile and could halve; INTC is a binary turnaround; healthcare faces policy risk. Energy and semis are both cyclical, so cross-correlations rise in a drawdown, and there is almost no defensive ballast other than staples and 6% cash. Over 24 months no rebalancing means winners grow and the book drifts into whatever wins, adding implicit concentration.

theses.title: Fiscal dominance and energy underinvestment keep real assets and pricing power valuable
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months, large fiscal deficits, persistent above-target inflation pressure, and a decade of upstream energy underinvestment keep real energy prices elevated and reward businesses with hard assets or pricing power; this is falsified if a global recession holds crude below roughly $55-60 for a sustained period or if inflation falls durably back to 2% with rate cuts crowding in capex.
theses.portfolioExpression: Concentrated integrated oil, oilfield services and pricing-power staples (XOM, CVX, SLB, MO, KO) plus a scarce digital asset (BTC) express the view that real assets and pricing power outperform long-duration financial claims.

theses.title: The 2026 AI-infrastructure drawdown prices an early end that does not come
theses.worldView: Hyperscaler and industrial AI capital spending broadens from accelerators into wafer-fab equipment, memory, foundry capacity and inference over the next 24 months; this is falsified if hyperscaler capex guidance falls year over year or if wafer-fab-equipment bookings keep contracting through 2027.
theses.portfolioExpression: Overweight semiconductor equipment, foundry and search/AI platforms that sold off hard (AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, TSM, GOOGL) while the long-run AI demand story is intact.

theses.title: US industrial policy and deglobalization sustain domestic manufacturing and compute capex
theses.worldView: Tariffs, CHIPS-style subsidies, grid and data-center buildouts, and strategic re-shoring keep US manufacturing and domestic semiconductor capacity spending elevated for two more years; this is falsified if policy support is repealed or if industrial capex falls broadly across 2027.
theses.portfolioExpression: Positions in domestic semiconductor capacity and legacy-process champions (INTC, TSM, AMAT) that directly monetize fab construction and onshored compute.

theses.title: Large-cap healthcare cash flows are underpriced after a multi-year de-rating
theses.worldView: Demographics, obesity/diabetes franchises and managed-care scale mean the big pharma and healthcare-services names generate durable cash flows at valuations the market has discounted for policy fear; this is falsified if US drug pricing policy or Medicare Advantage economics structurally impair these earnings streams.
theses.portfolioExpression: Modest but meaningful positions in diversified, cash-generative healthcare (CVS, PFE, BMY) bought after years of underperformance.

theses.title: Persistent deficits make non-sovereign scarce digital assets a two-year hedge
theses.worldView: With fiscal dominance and rising sovereign debt loads, a fixed-supply digital asset sees continued adoption from institutions and ETF wrappers over 24 months; this is falsified if regulatory prohibition, persistent ETF outflows, or a stablecoin/credit shock push BTC materially below its 52-week low and keeps it there.
theses.portfolioExpression: A combined roughly 12% exposure to spot BTC and ETH plus a small crypto-market-structure equity (HOOD) as a higher-beta expression.

pick.thesis: The book bets that the next two years look like an inflationary, capex-heavy, reindustrializing world rather than a disinflationary deflation: real assets and pricing power win (T1), AI infrastructure spending broadens after a punishing 2026 drawdown (T2), US policy keeps fabs and factories being built (T3), neglected healthcare cash flows re-rate (T4), and scarce digital assets hedge fiscal excess (T5). The tension is real: T1's inflation persistence argues against long-duration growth, while T2/T3 are growth-capex bets that would suffer in a recession; the weights resolve this by concentrating in cash-generative cyclicals (energy) and already-cheap hardware names rather than richly valued software, with only a small crypto sleeve for convexity.

forecasts.reason: Central estimate of roughly +28% total return over 24 months assumes the world I describe: energy stays supported by underinvestment and disciplined supply, AI capital spending broadens rather than collapses, US fab and factory capex continues, healthcare cash flows partially re-rate, and a scarce digital asset benefits from fiscal dominance. For this forecast to be plausible, no severe global recession occurs and semicap orders re-accelerate sometime in 2027; if a hard landing or a second AI capex bust arrives, the same portfolio could easily be down 25-40%, so this is a broad central guess with wide uncertainty, not a promise.

positions.name: Exxon Mobil
positions.thesis: A supermajor with low-cost upstream assets and chemical/downstream integration is the cleanest application of the view that disciplined capital allocation and underinvested global supply keep real crude and gas prices elevated; the snapshot shows it up about 61% over 12 months at 179.67 versus a 52-week high of 187.25, so this is buying a strong but not vertical tape within an energy regime I expect to persist, not chasing a proven bargain. It is the largest single position at 11% because it is the most direct, highest-quality expression of the primary thesis, which is tolerable under the high-risk mandate.
positions.catalyst: Sustained Brent above my implied $65-70 range, continued buybacks and dividend growth, and further Permian and Guyana project start-ups.
positions.invalidation: Crude sustained below roughly $55-60, a global demand collapse, or a capex spree that destroys free cash flow would invalidate both the world thesis and this application.

positions.name: Chevron
positions.thesis: The second integrated major diversifies the same world view: strong free cash flow from Permian and international assets plus downstream means it benefits from elevated real energy prices and inflationary pricing power; at 227.77 after a 54% twelve-month gain it sits just below its 52-week high of 235.52, which I accept as reasonable rather than distressed. Its 7% weight pairs with XOM to spread single-operator risk while keeping the energy thesis concentrated enough to matter.
positions.catalyst: Permian and Tengiz volume growth, disciplined buybacks, and any supply-side discipline from OPEC+ or sanctions enforcement.
positions.invalidation: A sustained sub-$60 crude environment or a major operational/regulatory loss in its key basins.

positions.name: SLB (Schlumberger)
positions.thesis: Oilfield services are the leveraged call on the same underinvestment view: if producers must drill more to replace depleted barrels, service pricing and international activity rise; at 52.31 it is well below its 52-week high of 59.79 despite a 47.5% twelve-month gain, so the market is pricing some activity risk I think is overstated. Its 5% weight reflects higher cyclicality and operating leverage than the majors, appropriate for high risk but capped.
positions.catalyst: Rising international and offshore drilling budgets, service price inflation, and data-center-driven gas demand pulling gas activity higher.
positions.invalidation: A drilling recession with rig counts falling year over year, or oilfield service pricing deflation.

positions.name: Applied Materials
positions.thesis: The largest wafer-fab-equipment maker is the core expression of my view that the 2026 semicap drawdown overprices an AI capex end: the snapshot shows it down 31% over three months at 374.53 versus a 52-week high of 722.23 while still up 62% over 12 months, a violent de-rating of a franchise tied to AI, HBM and onshored fabs; I assume equipment orders re-accelerate as CHIPS-funded and AI-driven fabs ramp. Its 7% weight is a large, contrarian position in a volatile name, consistent with high risk tolerance for drawdowns.
positions.catalyst: Rebounding WFE bookings, HBM and gate-all-around equipment demand, and new domestic fab announcements.
positions.invalidation: Year-over-year declines in WFE bookings through 2027 or hyperscaler capex guidance cuts.

positions.name: Lam Research
positions.thesis: Etch and deposition exposure to memory (especially HBM and DRAM) applies the same world view; at 227.56 it is down 28% over three months versus a 52-week high of 432.87 despite a 42% twelve-month gain, so the market has already cut a large fraction of the AI-memory cycle that I believe has more room to run. Its 6% weight keeps memory-cycle beta meaningful without doubling the semicap single-name risk beyond AMAT.
positions.catalyst: Memory makers raising capex on HBM and advanced DRAM demand from AI servers.
positions.invalidation: Memory makers cutting capex or an oversupply-driven memory price collapse.

positions.name: KLA Corporation
positions.thesis: Process control and inspection demand rises with every new complex fab node, so it is the quality expression of fab build-out; at 153.11 it is down 22% over three months versus a 301.37 high, a de-rating I attribute to capex-cycle fear rather than franchise loss. Its 5% weight adds a less commodity-like, higher-margin semicap name to the same thesis.
positions.catalyst: Advanced-node yield challenges requiring more inspection, plus new fab construction in the US and abroad.
positions.invalidation: A prolonged freeze in new fab construction or process-control spending.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.thesis: Search, cloud, and custom silicon make Alphabet a cash-generative application of the view that AI diffusion, not AI abandonment, drives the next two years; the snapshot shows it down 26% over three months at 278.99 and roughly flat over 12 months versus a 52-week high of 402.12, which I interpret as the market pricing disruption risk to search more aggressively than I believe is warranted over 24 months. I am assuming, not verifying, that its balance sheet and cash generation remain robust. Its 9% weight is the largest technology position, anchoring T2 as one of the more defensive cash-flow names in the book while accepting headline and regulatory risk.
positions.catalyst: Cloud and Gemini monetization growth, continued buybacks, or any resolution of regulatory overhang.
positions.invalidation: Sustained share loss in search queries and advertising revenue, or AI capex escalating without revenue follow-through.

positions.name: Intel
positions.thesis: This is the highest-risk expression of the reindustrialization thesis: a US process-technology and foundry turnaround is a bet that policy and strategic demand for domestic logic capacity persist; the snapshot shows it up 49% over 12 months at 59.97 but down 41% over three months from a 140.94 high, a pattern consistent with a volatile, headline-driven turnaround rather than a proven recovery. I assume foundry customer traction and node execution improve; this is the least verifiable claim in the book. Its 4% weight is deliberate lottery-ticket sizing so a near-total loss is painful but not portfolio-defining.
positions.catalyst: New foundry customers, successful node milestones, or additional government/strategic investment.
positions.invalidation: Further node delays, foundry customer losses, or failure to reach foundry breakeven.
